x: Commentary on Surah "Alhākum" [al-Takāthur] — In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
Commentary on the saying of the Exalted, glorified be His praise and hallowed His names:
h

Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1) until you visit the graves (2) No! You are going to know (3) Again, no! You are going to know (4) No! If you only knew with the knowledge of certainty (5) You will surely see the Blazing Fire (6) Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty (7) Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. The Exalted says: O people, boasting about abundance of wealth and numbers has distracted you from obedience to your Lord, and from what would save you from His wrath against you.
The interpreters said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah:
m: h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1) until you visit the graves (2)

. He said: They used to say: "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and we are [more countless than] (1) the sons of so-and-so." Every day they were dropping off, until the last of them. By God, they went on like that until all of them became people of the graves (2).

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah:
m: h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1)

. They said: "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so." That distracted them (1) until they died in error (2). Words were also reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, indicating that the meaning is rivalry in wealth.

x: Mention of the report on this:

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī, from Qatādah, from Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from his father,
m: that he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as he was reciting
h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1) until you visit the graves (2)
. He said: "Son of Adam, you have of your wealth only what you eat and consume, or wear and wear out, or give in charity and thereby send ahead" (3).

c: Muḥammad ibn Khalaf al-ʿAsqalānī narrated to us, saying: Ādam narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from Anas ibn Mālik, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said:
m: We used to think that this saying was part of the Qurʾān: "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would long for a third, and nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam but dust; then God turns in mercy to whoever repents" — until this surah was revealed:
h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1)
to its end (4).

x: The Prophet's statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, right after his recitation of
h
distracts you
: "You have of your wealth only such and such" indicates that, in his understanding, the meaning of
h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you
is: wealth.

evidence.text: The Prophet's statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, right after his recitation of {distracts you}: "You have of your wealth only such and such" indicates that, in his understanding, the meaning of {Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you} is: wealth.

x: And His saying:
h
until you visit the graves

. He means: until you end up in the graves and are buried in them. In this is evidence for the soundness of the doctrine of the punishment of the grave, because God, exalted be His mention, informed us regarding these people whom rivalry in increase distracted that they will come to know what they will meet when they visit the graves — as a warning and threat to them.
The interpreters said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah narrated to us, from Qays, from Ḥajjāj, from al-Minhāl, from Zirr, from ʿAlī, who said:
m: We used to doubt the punishment of the grave until this verse was revealed:
h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1)
up to
h
No! You are going to know (2)
— concerning the punishment of the grave.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥukkām ibn Salm narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Minhāl, from Zirr, from ʿAlī, who said:
m: h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1)
was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥukkām narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Zirr, from ʿAlī, who said:
m: We kept doubting the punishment of the grave until this was revealed:
h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you (1) until you visit the graves (2)

x: And His saying:
h
No! You are going to know (3)
. The Exalted means by His saying
h
No!
: it is not thus that you should act, that rivalry in increase should distract you.
And His saying:
h
You are going to know (3)

. He, glorified be His praise, says: you will come to know, when you visit the graves, O you whom rivalry in increase distracted, the outcome of what you did and of your being preoccupied in this world with rivalry in increase instead of obedience to your Lord (1).
And His saying:
h
Again, no! You are going to know (4)

. He says: Then, it is not thus that you should act, that rivalry in wealth and numbers should distract you; you will come to know, when you visit the graves, what you will meet — when you visit them — of the harm of your preoccupation with rivalry in increase over obedience to your Lord. He repeated His saying
h
No! You are going to know (4)
twice because, when the Arabs want to intensify a warning and a threat, they repeat the word twice.
Something was also reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk on this, which Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying:

c: Mihrān narrated to us, from Abū Sinān, from Thābit, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk:
m: h
No! You are going to know (4)
: He said: the disbelievers;
h
Again, no! You are going to know (4)
: He said: the believers. And so he used to recite it (2).

evidence.text: And so he used to recite it (2).

x: And His saying:
h
No! If you only knew with the knowledge of certainty (5)

. The Exalted says: it is not thus that you should act, that rivalry in increase should distract you, O people. If you knew, O people, with certain knowledge that God will resurrect you on the Day of Resurrection after your deaths from your graves, rivalry in increase would not have distracted you from obedience to God, your Lord; you would have hastened to worship Him, to heed His command and prohibition, and to abandon the world, out of fear for yourselves of His punishment.
The interpreters said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah:
m: h
No! If you only knew with the knowledge of certainty (5)
: We used to be told that the knowledge of certainty is for a person to know that God will resurrect him after death (1).

x: And His saying:
h
You will surely see the Blazing Fire (6)
. The reciters differed in the reading of this. The majority (2) of the reciters of the regions read
h
laturawunna al-jaḥīm (6)
with a fatḥah on the tāʾ of
h
laturawunna

in both instances (3), while al-Kisāʾī read it with a ḍammah on the tāʾ of the first and a fatḥah on the second (4). The correct reading in our view is the fatḥah in both, because of the consensus of the authorities on it. This being so, the meaning of the verse is: you will surely see Hell, O polytheists, on the Day of Resurrection; then you will surely see it plainly, never absent from it.

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: regarding His saying:
h
Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty (7)
: He means the people of polytheism.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of this.

The majority (2) of the reciters of the regions read {laturawunna al-jaḥīm (6)} with a fatḥah on the tāʾ of {laturawunna} in both instances (3), while al-Kisāʾī read it with a ḍammah on the tāʾ of the first and a fatḥah on the second (4).
The correct reading in our view is the fatḥah in both, because of the consensus of the authorities on it.

x: And His saying:
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)

. He says: then God, mighty and majestic, will surely ask you about the pleasure in which you lived in this world: what you did with it, from where you attained it, in what you acquired it, and what you did with it.
The interpreters differed about what that pleasure is.
Some of them said: it is security and health.
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAbbād ibn Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn Masʿūd,
m: regarding His saying
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. He said: Security and health (1).

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ḥafṣ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAbd Allāh,
m: likewise (2).

c: ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd al-Kindī narrated to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Marwān narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid:
m: h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. He said: Security and health (3).

c: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, saying:
m: It reached me regarding His saying
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. He said: Security and health.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said:
m: I heard al-Shaʿbī say: The pleasure about which one will be asked on the Day of Resurrection is security and health. He said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Khālid al-Zayyāt, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn Masʿūd, likewise. He said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān:
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. He said: Security and health.

x: Others said: rather, the meaning is: then they will be asked that Day about what God bestowed on them, namely the hearing, sight and bodily health He granted them.
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: regarding His saying
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. He said: The pleasure is the health of bodies, hearing and sight. He said: God will ask His servants on what they used them, though He knows that better than they do; that is His saying:
h
Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart — about all of those one will be questioned
(1) [al-Isrāʾ: 36].

c: Ismāʿīl ibn Mūsā al-Fazārī narrated to me, saying: ʿUmar ibn Shākir informed us, from al-Ḥasan,
m: who used to say regarding His saying
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. He said: Hearing, sight and bodily health.

x: Others said: it is well-being (ʿāfiyah).
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAbbād ibn Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Nūḥ ibn Darrāj narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf, from Abū Jaʿfar:
m: h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure (8)
. He said: Well-being.

x: Others said: rather, what is meant is some of what a person eats or drinks.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn ʿAtīq, who said:
m: I saw Saʿīd ibn Jubayr brought a drink of honey; he drank it and said: This is the pleasure about which you will be asked (1).

c: ʿAlī ibn Sahl al-Ramlī narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Bilāl narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us,
m: from ʿAmmār (2) ibn Abī ʿAmmār, who said: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both; we fed them fresh dates and gave them water to drink, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "This is part of the pleasure about which you will be asked" (3).

c: Jābir ibn al-Kurdī narrated to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār, who said:
m: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us. Then he mentioned something similar. Al-Ḥusayn (4) ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣudāʾī narrated to me, saying:

c: al-Walīd ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Kaysān, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayrah, who said:
m: While Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both, were sitting, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and said: "What has made you sit here?" [They said: Hunger] (1). He said: "By Him who sent me with the truth, nothing else brought me out." So they set out until they came to the house of a man of the Anṣār, and his wife met them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: "Where is so-and-so?" She said: He went to fetch us sweet water. Then their host came carrying his waterskin and said: Welcome! No servants have ever been visited by anything better than what has visited me today. He hung his waterskin on the base of the palm fronds (2) of a date palm, went off, and came back with a cluster of dates. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Could you not have picked for us?" He said: I wanted you to choose for yourselves, under your own eyes. Then he took the knife, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Beware of the milch animal." So he slaughtered for them that day, and they ate. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "You will be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your houses, and you did not return until you had obtained this; this is part of the pleasure" (3).

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Shaybān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar: "Come with us to Abū al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihān al-Anṣārī." They came to him, and he took them to the shade of his orchard and spread a mat for them. Then he went to a palm tree and came with a cluster of dates, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Why did you not pick out for us from its ripe dates?" He said: I wanted you to choose (4) from its ripe and its unripe dates. They ate and drank water, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished, he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this is part of the pleasure about which you will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: this cool shade and cool dates, with cool water on them."

c: Ṣāliḥ ibn Misḥār al-Marwazī narrated to me, saying: Ādam ibn Abī Iyās narrated to us, saying: Shaybān narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to us, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly, except that he said in his report: "cool shade, cool ripe dates, and cool water" (1).

c: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā al-Bazzāz narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from Ḥashraj ibn Nubātah,
m: saying: Abū Nuṣayrah (2) narrated to us, from Abū ʿAsīb, the freedman of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by [at night, and called me, so I went out to him; then he passed by Abū Bakr and called him, and he went out to him, then by ʿUmar; then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on] (3) until he entered an orchard belonging to one of the Anṣār. He said to the owner of the orchard: "Feed us unripe dates." He brought a cluster and placed it down, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions ate. Then he asked for cold water and drank, and said: "You will be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection." ʿUmar took the cluster and struck the ground with it until the unripe dates scattered, and then said: O Messenger of God, will we really be asked about this? He said: "Yes, except for a piece of bread with which he stops his hunger, or a burrow into which he enters from the heat and the cold" (4).

c: Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr al-Sakūnī narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Ḥashraj ibn Nubātah, who said:
m: Abū Nuṣayrah (1) narrated to me, from Abū ʿAsīb, the freedman of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by me and called me, so I went out, with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both, accompanying him. He entered an orchard belonging to one of the Anṣār, and a cluster of its unripe dates was brought and placed before him. He ate, he and his Companions, then asked for cold water and drank. Then he said: "You will be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection." ʿUmar said: About this, on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "Yes, except for three things: a piece of cloth with which he covers his nakedness, a piece of bread with which he stills his hunger (2), or a burrow into which he enters from the heat and the cold."

c: Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from al-Jurayrī, from Abū Nuṣayrah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of his Companions ate a meal of unsifted barley bread with fatty meat, and then drank from a stream. He said: "[This is a meal] (3) of the pleasure (4) about which you will be asked (5) on the Day of Resurrection" (6).

c: Mujāhid ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym,
m: from (7) Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, who said: When
h
Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you
was revealed, and he recited it until he reached
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure

, they said: O Messenger of God, about which pleasure will we be asked, when all we have are the two black things, water and dates, our swords on our shoulders, and the enemy at hand? He said: "That will come to pass" (8).

c: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣudāʾī narrated to me,
m: both saying: Shabābah ibn Sawwār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-ʿAlāʾ Abū Zabr (1) al-Shāmī narrated to me, saying: al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn ʿArzam narrated to us, saying: I heard Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The first thing a servant will be asked about of the pleasure on the Day of Resurrection is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and quench your thirst with cool water?" (2).
b.via: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣudāʾī

c: Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Mujāhid, who said: Abū Maʿmar ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sakhbarah said:
m: Nobody wakes up in Kufa except in comfort; the humblest of them in livelihood is the one who eats wheat bread, drinks the water of the Euphrates and takes shade in the shade, and that is part of the pleasure (3).
b.via: Abū Maʿmar ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sakhbarah

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith al-Tamīmī, from Thābit al-Bunānī, from the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "The pleasure about which one will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: a piece of bread that strengthens him, water that quenches his thirst, and a garment that covers him" (4). He said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Bishr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yasār (5), who said: I heard some of the people of Yemen say: I heard Abū Umāmah say: The pleasure about which one will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: wheat bread and sweet water. He said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Bukayr ibn ʿAtīq al-ʿĀmirī, who said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr was brought a drink of honey, and he said: This is indeed part of (1) the pleasure about which we will be asked on the Day of Resurrection:
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Bukayr ibn ʿAtīq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
m: that he was brought a drink of honey and said: This is part of the pleasure about which you will be asked (2).

x: Others said: it is everything a person enjoyed in the world.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding the saying of God
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure
. He said: About everything of the enjoyment of this world (3).

c: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah,
m: regarding His saying
h
Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure
: God, mighty and majestic, will ask every servant about what He entrusted to him of His blessing and His due.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah:
m: h
You will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure

. He said: God, exalted be His mention, will ask everyone who had a blessing about what He bestowed upon him. Al-Ḥasan and Qatādah used to say: There are three things about which the son of Adam will not be asked, while everything besides them is subject to questioning and reckoning, except as God wills: a garment with which he covers his nakedness, a piece of bread with which he supports his back, and a house that shades him (1). The correct position on this is to say: God informed us that He will ask these people about the pleasure, and He did not specify in His statement that He will ask them about one kind of pleasure rather than another; rather, His statement is general, covering all of it. So He will ask them, as He said, about all pleasure, not some of it to the exclusion of the rest. End of the commentary on Surah "Alhākum".

evidence.text: Mujāhid ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, from (7) Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, who said: When {Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you} was revealed, and he recited it until he reached {Then you will surely be asked that Day about the pleasure}, they said: O Messenger of God, about which pleasure will we be asked, when all we have are the two black things, water and dates, our swords on our shoulders, and the enemy at hand?

notes.en: Manuscripts S and T1 read “aqdam”; T2 and T3 read “aʿdam”; al-Waraʿ reads “aʿazz min.” The adopted reading agrees with Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir. “Aʿaddu min” means “greater in number.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1: "أقدم"، وفى ت 2، ت 3: "أعدم"، وفى الورع: "أعز من". والمثبت موافق لما في تفسير ابن كثير، وأعد من: أي: أكثر عددا.

notes.en: Ahmad mentioned it in Kitab al-Waraʿ (p. 189) from Shayban, from Qatadah. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/493).
notes.ar: ذكره أحمد في كتاب الورع ص 189 عن شيبان، عن قتادة، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 493.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T2, and T3 read “alhakum.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ت 3: "ألهاكم".

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/393) from Maʿmar with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/387) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 393 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 387 إلى عبد حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ahmad (26/232–233, no. 16305) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Adab (no. 1110) transmitted it through Wakiʿ. Al-Tayalisi (no. 1244), Muslim (no. 2958), al-Tahawi in al-Mushkil (no. 1657), Ibn Hibban (no. 3327), al-Hakim (2/533–534), Abu Nuʿaym in Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ (6/281), and al-Khatib in his Tarikh (1/359) transmitted it through Hisham. Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd (no. 497), Ahmad (26/233–234, no. 16306), ʿAbd ibn Humayd (no. 513), al-Tirmidhi (nos. 2342, 2354), al-Nasaʾi (no. 3615), al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (no. 2888), and al-Hakim (4/61) transmitted it through Qatadah. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/386) to Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 26/ 232، 233 (16305)، والبيهقى في الآداب (1110) من طريق وكيع به، وأخرجه الطيالسي (1244)، ومسلم (2958)، والطحاوى في المشكل (1657)، وابن حبان (3327)، والحاكم 2/ 533، 534، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 6/ 281، والخطيب في تاريخه 1/ 359 من طريق هشام به، وأخرجه ابن المبارك في الزهد (497)، وأحمد 26/ 233، 234 (16306)، وعبد بن حميد (513)، والترمذى (2342، 2354)، والنسائي (3615)، والطبراني في الأوسط (2888)، والحاكم 4/ 61 من طريق قتادة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 386 إلى سعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Al-Bukhari transmitted it (no. 6440) through Hammad ibn Salama with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى (6440) من طريق حماد بن سلمة به.

notes.en: Al-Tirmidhi (no. 3355) and Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir—as cited in Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir (8/494)—transmitted it through Hakam. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/387) to Khushaysh ibn Asram in al-Istiqama, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه الترمذى (3355)، وابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 8/ 494 - من طريق حكام به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 387 إلى خشيش بن أصرم في الاستقامة وابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “Allah” after it.
notes.ar: بعده في م: "الله".

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/494). Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/387) to the author.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 494، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 387 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/392) from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, with a similar wording. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/387) to al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 392 عن معمر، عن قتادة بنحوه، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 387 إلى الفريابي وابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Manuscript M omits it.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: This is the reading of Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, ʿAsim, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, Abu Jaʿfar, Yaʿqub, and Khalaf. See al-Nashr (2/301).
notes.ar: وبها قرأ نافع وابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وخلف. ينظر النشر 2/ 301.

notes.en: This is the reading of Ibn ʿAmir. See the preceding source.
notes.ar: وبها قرأ ابن عامر. المصدر السابق.

notes.en: ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad transmitted it in Zawaʾid al-Zuhd (p. 157), and Ibn Abi Hatim—as cited in Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir (8/497)—through Muhammad ibn Sulayman, as a report raised to the Prophet.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الله بن أحمد في زاوئد الزهد ص 157، وابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 8/ 497 - من طريق محمد بن سليمان به مرفوعًا.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Shuʿab (no. 4615) through Hafs. Hunad transmitted it in al-Zuhd (no. 694) from Hafs, from Ibn Abi Layla, who attributed it to Ibn Masʿud. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/388) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب (4615) من طريق حفص به، وأخرجه هناد في الزهد (694) عن حفص عن ابن أبي ليلى يرفعه إلى ابن مسعود، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 388 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Al-Tusi mentioned it in al-Tibyan (10/403).
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسي في التبيان 10/ 403.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Shuʿab (no. 4613) through Abu Salih with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/387–388) to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في الشعب (4613) من طريق أبي صالح به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 387، 388 إلى ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: The source references will be given on p. 610.
notes.ar: سيأتي تخريجه في ص 610.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T read “ʿImran.” The correct form appears in the following report.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت: "عمران". وسيأتي على الصواب في الأثر التالي.

notes.en: Al-Tayalisi (no. 1908), Ahmad (23/8, 378; nos. 14637, 15206), al-Nasaʾi (no. 3641), Abu Yaʿla (nos. 1790, 2161), al-Tahawi in al-Mushkil (nos. 470–471), Ibn Hibban (no. 3411), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (nos. 4599, 4600, 5877) transmitted it through Hammad ibn Salama. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/288) to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطاليسي (1908)، وأحمد 23/ 8، 378 (14637، 15206)، والنسائي (3641)، وأبو يعلى (1790، 2161)، والطحاوى في المشكل (470، 471)، وابن حبان (3411)، والبيهقى في الشعب (4599، 4600، 5877) من طريق حماد بن سلمة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 288 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “al-Hasan”; this has appeared several times earlier.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "الحسن"، وتقدم مرارًا.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 omit it.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3.

notes.en: Karb al-nakhl refers to the bases of the palm fronds. See Lisan al-ʿArab, root k-r-b.
notes.ar: كرب النخل: أصول السعف. اللسان (ك ر ب).

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/495) from the author. Muslim (no. 2038), Ibn Majah (no. 3180) in abbreviated form, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (no. 4602) transmitted it through Yazid ibn Kaysan.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسير 8/ 495 عن المصنف، وأخرجه مسلم (2038)، وابن ماجه (3180) مختصرًا، والبيهقى في الشعب (4602) من طريق يزيد بن كيسان به.

notes.en: Manuscripts S and T1 read “takhayyar”; T2 and T3 read “tatakhayyar.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1: "تخير"، وفى ت 2، ت 3: "تتخير".

notes.en: Al-Bukhari transmitted it in al-Adab al-Mufrad (no. 256) in abbreviated form; al-Tirmidhi (no. 2369), al-Hakim (4/131), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (no. 4604) transmitted it through Adam ibn Abi Iyas. Al-Tahawi in al-Mushkil (no. 472) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (no. 4603) transmitted it through Shayban. Al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11697) transmitted it through ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr in abbreviated form. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/389) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخاري في الأدب المفرد (256) مختصرًا، والترمذى (2369)، والحاكم 4/ 131، والبيهقى في الشعب (4604) من طريق آدم بن أبي إياس به، وأخرجه الطحاوى في المشكل (472)، والبيهقي في الشعب (4603) من طريق شيبان به، وأخرجه النَّسَائِي في الكبرى (11697) من طريق عبد الملك بن عمير به مختصرًا، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 389 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “Basira.” He is Muslim ibn ʿUbayd; see his biographical entry in Tahdhib al-Kamal (34/345).
notes.ar: في النسخ: "بصيرة". وهو مسلم بن عبيد. ينظر ترجمته في تهذيب الكمال 34/ 345.

notes.en: Manuscript M omits it.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: Ibn ʿAdi transmitted it in al-Kamil (2/847) through Saʿid ibn Sulayman. Ahmad (5/81), al-Tahawi in al-Mushkil (nos. 468–469), al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (no. 4601), Ibn Manda—as cited in al-Isaba (7/275)—and Ibn ʿAsakir in Tarikh Dimashq (4/134, 295–296) transmitted it through Hashraj ibn Nubata. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/389) to al-Baghawi in his Muʿjam and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن عدى في الكامل 2/ 847 من طريق سعيد بن سليمان به، وأخرجه أحمد 5/ 81، والطحاوى في المشكل (468، 469)، والبيهقى في الشعب (4601)، وابن منده - كما في الإصابة 7/ 275 - وابن عساكر في تاريخ دمشق 4/ 134، 295، 296 من طريق حشرج بن نباتة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 389 إلى البغوي في معجمه وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, M, T2, and T3 read “Basira”; T1 reads “Nasra.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت،2، ت:3 "بصيرة"، وفي ت 1: "نصرة".

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “juʿahu.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "جوعه".

notes.en: Manuscripts M, T2, and T read “hadha kulluhu” (“all of this”).
notes.ar: في م، ت 2 ت: "هذا كله".

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “alladhi” (“which”) after it.
notes.ar: بعده في م: "الذي".

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “ʿanhu” (“from him”) after it.
notes.ar: في م: "عنه".

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba transmitted it in his Musannaf (13/232–233) from Ibn ʿUlayya with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة في مصنفه 13/ 232، 233 عن ابن علية به.

notes.en: The manuscripts add “Muhammad ibn” after it; the established text follows the sources that document the report.
notes.ar: بعده في النسخ: "محمد بن"، والمثبت من مصادر التخريج.

notes.en: Ahmad transmitted it (5/429) from Yazid. Ibn Abi Shayba (13/231), Hunad in al-Zuhd (no. 768), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (no. 4598) transmitted it through Muhammad ibn ʿAmr. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/388) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 5/ 429 عن يزيد به، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 231، وهناد في الزهد (768)، والبيهقى في الشعب (4598) من طريق محمد بن عمرو به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 388 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “Razin.” The adopted form follows the sources that document the report; see Tahdhib al-Kamal (15/405–406).
notes.ar: في النسخ: "رزين". والمثبت من مصادر التخريج، وينظر تهذيب الكمال 15/ 405، 406.

notes.en: Yahya ibn Maʿin mentioned it in his Tarikh (al-Duri recension, 3/19). ʿAbd ibn Humayd—as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/388)—transmitted it; through him al-Tirmidhi (no. 3358), al-Baghawi in his Tafsir (8/519), ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawaʾid al-Zuhd (p. 31), and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/138) and Maʿrifat ʿUlum al-Hadith (p. 187) transmitted it through Shababa. Ibn Hibban (no. 7364) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (no. 4607) transmitted it through ʿAbdullah ibn al-ʿAlaʾ. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه يحيى بن معين في تاريخه (رواية الدورى) 3/ 19، وعبد بن حميد - كما في الدر المنثور 6/ 388 - ومن طريقه الترمذى (3358)، والبغوى في تفسيره 8/ 519، وعبد الله بن أحمد في زوائد الزهد ص 31، والحاكم في المستدرك 4/ 138، وفي معرفة علوم الحديث ص 187 من طريق شبابة به، وأخرجه ابن حبان (7364)، والبيهقي في الشعب (4607) من طريق عبد الله بن العلاء به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba transmitted it in his Musannaf (13/285), Ahmad in Fadaʾil al-Sahaba (no. 883), and Hunad in al-Zuhd (no. 699) through Layth, from Mujahid, from ʿAbdullah, from ʿAli. Al-Hakim transmitted it (2/445) through al-Aʿmash, from Mujahid, as a statement of ʿAli. Al-Suyuti similarly attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/388) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة في مصنفه 13/ 285، وأحمد في فضائل الصحابة (883)، وهناد في الزهد (699) من طريق ليث، عن مجاهد، عن عبد الله، عن علي، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 445 من طريق الأعمش، عن مجاهد به من قول على، وكذا عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 388 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/388) to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 388 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “Bashshar.” See Tahdhib al-Kamal (4/133).
notes.ar: في م: "بشار". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 4/ 133.

notes.en: Manuscript M omits it.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: Hunad transmitted it in al-Zuhd (no. 700) from Wakiʿ with this chain. Ibn Abi Shayba (13/538), Ahmad in al-Zuhd (p. 371), Hunad in al-Zuhd (no. 693), and Abu Nuʿaym in Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ (4/281) transmitted a similar report through Bukayr, with the addition that he drank it while enjoying it.
notes.ar: أخرجه هناد في الزهد (700) عن وكيع به، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 538، وأحمد في الزهد ص 371، وهناد في الزهد (693)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 281 من طريق بكير به نحوه، بزيادة: أنه شربه وهو يستلذ به.

notes.en: Al-Firyabi—as cited in al-Tamhid (24/343)—transmitted it through Warqaʾ. Abu Nuʿaym transmitted it in Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ (3/281) through Ibn Abi Najih and (3/298) through Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/388) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه الفريابي - كما في التمهيد 24/ 343 - عن ورقاء به، وأخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية 3/ 281 من طريق ابن أبي نجيح به، وفى 3/ 298 من طريق ابن جريج عن مجاهد، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 388 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ahmad mentioned it in Kitab al-Waraʿ (p. 188) from Maʿmar at length. ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/393) from Maʿmar, from al-Hasan and Qatadah.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد في كتاب الورع ص 188 من طريق معمر به مطولًا، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 393 عن معمر، عن الحسن وقتادة.
